solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hurt when losing millions, political party is financially embarrassed

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the word for hurt

parts.note: to hurt is to harm
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A politician's party, injured by losing its big-money backers, is left short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when losing' takes the M of millions out of HARM, leaving HAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone short of money is said to be hard up, which is being financially embarrassed.

clue.text: Artist wears an acceptable jacket

indicators.note: the artist is said to wear the word for acceptable, so that word goes round the artist like clothing

parts.note: OK means acceptable
RA is a Royal Academician, a standard crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter is dressed in a perfectly passable coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooded waterproof jacket: the anorak is a kind of weatherproof coat, so the general term fits.

clue.text: Naughty lady is in place of vice — one of seven baddies

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed in the den, the word for a place of vice

parts.note: a den is a haunt of vice, as in a den of iniquity

indicators.note: naughty suggests the letters are behaving badly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked woman is installed in a house of ill repute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' looks like a description of the lady but signals the rearrangement; 'in' then sets those shuffled letters inside the den.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian teaching lists seven deadly sins such as pride and greed, so each is one of seven baddies.

clue.text: Flirt quietly greeting one arriving at airport?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
hi is a greeting
a lander is something that lands, as an aircraft does arriving at an airport

explanation.surface: A softly spoken hello to a passenger just off a plane might be the start of a flirtation.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to philander is to flirt or have casual affairs, so the two verbs swap.

clue.text: Saint consecrates water inadequate for total immersion?

parts.note: to hallow is to make holy, or consecrate

explanation.surface: A saint blesses water that turns out too skimpy for a full-body baptism.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests baptism by total immersion; the definition is simply water too shallow to go under in.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: shallow water is too low to submerge in completely, hence inadequate for total immersion.

clue.text: Society needs money — first of rules from sociologist

parts.note: pence are British coins, so money

indicators.note: first of picks out only the opening letter of the word rules

explanation.surface: A society needs cash, says a sociologist, before it can lay down any rules.
explanation.walkthrough: PENCE are the small coins of British money.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Spencer was a Victorian English philosopher and sociologist, so the surname names one.

clue.text: Angel or archangel avoiding Great Britain

indicators.note: avoiding means the archangel's name must go without the two letters for Great Britain

parts.note: Gabriel is the archangel of the Annunciation

explanation.surface: Is that an angel or archangel giving Britain a wide berth?
explanation.walkthrough: GB is removed letter by letter: the G from the front and the B from the middle of GABRIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is named as an angel in Jewish and Christian tradition, and is also a spirit in Shakespeare's Tempest.

clue.text: Amorous type wanting maiden under fifty?

indicators.note: in a down answer the over sits beneath the fifty, so under places it second

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
in cricket a maiden is a maiden over, one bowled without a run scored, so maiden can stand for an over

explanation.surface: A man in search of a young woman, still under fifty?
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: an over is six balls, and a maiden is an over with no runs; this cricketing sense is easy to miss behind the romantic surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lover is a person in love, a romantically inclined type.

clue.text: Crude, dull, heartless quarrel set up conflict far and wide

indicators.note: in a down answer set up means the whole assembled string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: raw means crude, unrefined

indicators.note: heartless strips the middle letters from dull, keeping its two ends

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A rough, dreary, soulless argument gets started.
explanation.walkthrough: RAW + DL + ROW is RAWDLROW, which 'set up' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A global war is a conflict spread across many countries, fought far and wide.

clue.text: Gift, nothing new, put in case

indicators.note: put in places the zero and the abbreviation for new inside the grammatical case

parts.note: the dative is a grammatical case
O, zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A present, not brand new, is packed into a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is grammar, not a box: the DATIVE case.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal noun: a donative is a gift or donation, especially an official one.

clue.text: Lazy, very stuck in? Reverse

indicators.note: stuck in shows the abbreviation for very lodged within the word for lazy

parts.note: inert means inactive, lazy

explanation.surface: Someone idle stays home and refuses to move forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to invert something is to turn it upside down or reverse it.

clue.text: When there's a setback, see everyone 'oard food

indicators.note: a setback signals that the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: all means everyone
a hoard is a heap; with the aitch dropped, as the apostrophe shows, heap becomes 'eap

explanation.surface: A Cockney looks over everyone's stockpile of grub after a reversal of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'oard tells you to drop it from the synonym too: HEAP becomes EAP. ALL + EAP read backwards gives the answer; 'see' just points the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: paella is a Spanish rice dish with seafood or chicken, a kind of food.

clue.text: See journey taken by children in compound

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Look at the outing the kids went on to the chemistry lab.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry: a chloride is a compound of chlorine with another element.

clue.text: Bird not high up first to reach ground

indicators.note: in a down answer the top letter is sent to the bottom, so the first letter reaches the ground

parts.note: low means not high up

explanation.surface: A bird flying low is first to land.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the owl is a nocturnal bird of prey.

clue.text: New release — diary that covers a bit more than the 365 days

definitions.text: that covers a bit more than the 365 days

indicators.note: new signals that the words are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly released diary covering the year is advertised.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy: the year measured against the fixed stars is about 365 days 6 hours 9 minutes, slightly longer than a calendar year.

clue.text: Hostility of worker having pay hit badly

parts.note: the ant is the classic crossword worker

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A labourer is resentful after his wages are cut hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: antipathy is deep dislike or aversion, close to hostility.

clue.text: Cry out over nothing — Nato countries becoming most fearful?

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
O, zero, means nothing
the West is the bloc of Western nations allied in Nato

explanation.surface: Protesting about nothing, the Western alliance looks very frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' only joins the cry to what follows. Yellow is slang for cowardly, so the most yellow is the most fearful; the question mark flags the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: yellow means cowardly, so the superlative is the most cowardly or fearful.

clue.text: Troubles in obscure land rising

indicators.note: in places the word for troubles inside the word for obscure

parts.note: to hide is to obscure
ills are troubles

explanation.surface: Unrest in a remote country is on the increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a slope of ground going up a hill is land that is rising.

clue.text: A clarinet op. — unusual to have one in it?

definitions.text: A clarinet op. — unusual to have one in it?

indicators.note: in it means a letter is put inside the rearranged letters just made
unusual tells us the letters appear in an unusual arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the abbreviation for opus
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clarinet piece would be an odd item on a programme for a solo keyboard concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges A CLARINET OP and 'to have one in it' adds I among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo keyboard concert is the very place where a clarinet opus would be unexpected, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Valuable stuff making money for Scandinavians

definitions.meaning: rock mined for its valuable metal content
the öre is a small coin of Sweden, and öre or øre in Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Riches that make Scandinavians money.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: mined rock holding metal, and the hundredth part of a Scandinavian krona or krone.

clue.text: Prince is cleaner little boy

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner
Les is a short form of Leslie, a boy's name

explanation.surface: The prince turns out to be the son of a domestic help.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is British for a hired cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Charles was long the Prince of Wales before becoming King.

clue.text: Go back to compensate for dead grass, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is said aloud and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: to reseed a lawn is to sow it again where grass has died

explanation.surface: Should we return to replace the lawn that has died off?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to recede is to move back or withdraw, as a tide or hairline does.

clue.text: Country person looking untidy, the reverse of tip-top

parts.note: a sloven is a habitually untidy, careless person

indicators.note: the reverse of tells us to read the word for tip-top backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; in crosswords it is often written AI

explanation.surface: A scruffy rustic is anything but first-class.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first-class, is read as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Slovenia is a European country bordering Italy, Austria, Hungary and Croatia.

clue.text: 6.50 — soldier enters for watch

indicators.note: the soldier enters, going inside the numerals

parts.note: in Roman numerals six is VI and fifty is L
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: At ten to seven a soldier reports for guard duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 6.50 looks like a time but is read as Roman numerals VI and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a vigil is a period of keeping watch, often through the night.

clue.text: When turning up they may get some embarrassed, unsurprisingly!

definitions.text: When turning up they may get some embarrassed, unsurprisingly!

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up reads the letters from bottom to top
some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Unclothed figures appearing unexpectedly are bound to make a few people blush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes SEDUN from the end of 'embarrassed' and start of 'unsurprisingly'; 'turning up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclad people or pictures of them turning up are the sort of thing that would embarrass some onlookers.

clue.text: Bird quietly sitting by mate?

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
a lover is a partner or mate

explanation.surface: A bird sits silently beside its partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the plover is a wading bird of shores and fields.

clue.text: Scolded in the manner of a judge

definitions.meaning: told off; to wig someone is an old informal verb for reprimanding

definitions.text: in the manner of a judge
definitions.meaning: wearing a wig, as British judges do in court

explanation.surface: Told off, as a judge might do it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: reprimanded, and wearing the wig worn by a British judge on the bench.

clue.text: Machine very hot and covered with foam

parts.note: a lathe is a machine tool for turning wood or metal
red-hot, so red means very hot

explanation.surface: An overheating machine is coated with froth.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lathered means covered in foam, as from soap or a sweating horse.

clue.text: Not for them the fantasies liars set out

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out in a different order

explanation.surface: Fibbers have their fanciful stories exposed as fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: people who see things as they are have no time for fantasies or daydreams.

clue.text: Tiresome talk to get treaty fixed

indicators.note: fixed suggests the word has been rearranged or reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Endless chatter is needed to get a treaty sorted.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal noun: yatter is incessant idle chatter, talk that wearies the listener.
